title: Gan–Gross–Prasad restriction and period theory for classical groups
summary: Relative classical models, multiplicity and epsilon-character selection, classical conjecture propositions, and proved all-place endoscopic unitary nonvanishing and refined periods (GGP.8).

layers.title: Relative classical pairs and their subgroups

targets.name: GGP.RelevantPair
targets.title: Relevance of an inclusion
targets.statement: Define a relevant pair as an isometric inclusion W ↪ V with nondegenerate image, complement C, epsilon·(−1)^rank(C) = −1, and a maximal isotropic submodule of C of rank floor(rank(C)/2). An odd complement includes its residual nonisotropic line; the ambient V need not be split.
hypotheses: F is a field with 2 invertible; A is F with identity involution or a quadratic étale F-algebra with its canonical involution; epsilon ∈ {1,−1}; all form modules are finite free and nondegenerate

locator.where: §2, pp. 5–7; ggp line 179, ggp line 229

api.name: GGP.RelevantPair.mkOfWittDecomposition
api.statement: A decomposition C = X ⊕ X∨ in the skew case, or X ⊕ L ⊕ X∨ in the symmetric case with L nonisotropic, constructs the pair.

api.name: GGP.RelevantPair.ext
api.statement: Two witnesses on the same isometric inclusion define the same relevance proposition.

api.name: GGP.RelevantPair.transport
api.statement: Isometries of both spaces commuting with the inclusion preserve relevance; identity and composition agree.

api.name: GGP.RelevantPair.codim_parity

tests.name: relevant_anisotropic_line
tests.statement: The inclusion 0 ↪ ⟨1⟩ over R is relevant; the real positive plane as complement of 0 fails both odd parity and splitness.

tests.name: relevant_nonsplit_even_complement

tests.name: alternating_orientation_witness
tests.statement: On the alternating plane B(e,f) = 1 and B(f,e) = −1; the reversed orientation changes the Heisenberg commutator sign in §2.2.

targets.name: GGP.relativeSubgroup
targets.title: The flag subgroup and its embedding
targets.statement: For a relevant pair and a complete flag in X in a Witt decomposition of its complement, construct P = stabilizer(flag), N = Ru(P), and H = N ⋊ G(W); construct the closed embedding j(n,g) = (n·i(g),g) into G(V) × G(W), where i(g) acts trivially on the complement and G means the connected isometry group.
hypotheses: F is a field with 2 invertible; A is F with identity involution or a quadratic étale F-algebra with its canonical involution; epsilon ∈ {1,−1}; all form modules are finite free and nondegenerate
A relevant pair and a complete isotropic flag as in §1.1

api.name: GGP.relativeSubgroup_apply
api.statement: The two coordinate formulas are j(n,g).1 = n·i(g) and j(n,g).2 = g.

api.name: GGP.relativeSubgroup_ker_projection

api.name: GGP.relativeSubgroup_congr
api.statement: A compatible change of Witt flag induces conjugate subgroup embeddings, with identity/composition coherence.

tests.statement: For a one-dimensional symmetric complement X = 0, N = 1 and j is the diagonal smaller group; including extra unipotents would fail.

tests.name: relativeSubgroup_codim_zero

tests.name: relativeSubgroup_two_coordinates
tests.statement: For n = 1 in the unipotent radical and any g, j(1,g) = (i(g),g), whereas j(u,1) = (u,1); this distinguishes product from diagonal projections.

targets.proofSketch: Restrict the imported parabolic Levi action to G(W); prove it normalizes Ru(P). Use the semidirect universal property and projection to prove injectivity.

targets.name: GGP.IsRelevantInnerForm
targets.title: Relevance across pure inner forms
targets.statement: For a pure inner twist of G(V) × G(W) represented by form spaces (V′,W′), define relevance by existence of a nondegenerate isometric inclusion W′ ↪ V′ whose complement is isometric to C = W⊥. Retain pure-twist markings when constructing packet members; do not identify every form of equal rank.
hypotheses: F is a field with 2 invertible; A is F with identity involution or a quadratic étale F-algebra with its canonical involution; epsilon ∈ {1,−1}; all form modules are finite free and nondegenerate
The original relevant pair and an actual pure inner twist supplied by the classification

api.name: GGP.IsRelevantInnerForm.refl

api.name: GGP.IsRelevantInnerForm.transport

api.name: GGP.IsRelevantInnerForm.complement

tests.name: inner_zero_complement
tests.statement: For C = 0 in an equal-rank skew pair, relevance requires V′ ≅ W′; equal dimensions alone do not suffice.

tests.name: inner_real_complement
tests.statement: Take W to be a positive real line and V of signature (3,1), with split complement C of signature (2,1). In the pure inner twist V′ of signature (1,3), a positive W′ has negative-definite three-dimensional complement. The dimensions and discriminants of V′,W′ match V,W, but this complement is not isometric to C; relevance fails.

tests.name: inner_split_GL
tests.statement: For A = F × F, pure inner forms of the GL factors are trivial; counting central simple algebra inner forms as pure twists gives a wrong extra member.

targets.name: GGP.splitPairEquiv
targets.title: The split quadratic-algebra comparison
targets.statement: For A = F × F with swap involution, identify V with V0 ⊕ V0∨ as an A-module with its evaluation epsilon-form; restriction to V0 identifies G(V) with GL(V0), and identifies j(H) and the relative form constructions with the GL Bessel/Fourier–Jacobi constructions of §13. Its character identification uses generating residual vectors and factorwise nontrivial additive characters as in §2.1, and unimodular Fourier–Jacobi functionals as in §2.2; it does not identify degenerate data with the generic GL model.
hypotheses: F is a field with 2 invertible; A is F with identity involution or a quadratic étale F-algebra with its canonical involution; epsilon ∈ {1,−1}; all form modules are finite free and nondegenerate
A = F × F, a chosen split-module decomposition and a relevant pair

tests.name: split_line_inverse
tests.statement: For V0 = F and a ∈ Fˣ, the isometry is (a,a⁻¹); taking (a,a) fails preservation for a² ≠ 1.

tests.name: split_rank_zero

targets.proofSketch: The second factor is forced to be inverse dual by the perfect pairing; evaluate on each idempotent of A. Compute the flag stabilizer and its radical in these coordinates.

layers.title: Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi models

targets.name: GGP.besselCharacter
targets.title: Bessel characters
targets.statement: For epsilon = +1 and complement X ⊕ L ⊕ X∨, choose e generating the free residual A-line L (so B(e,e) ∈ Fˣ), a basis v1,…,vr of X and dual vectors v′i. For r > 0 define l(u) = sum(i=1,…,r−1) B(u·v(i+1),v′i) + B(u·e,v′r) and nu(u,g) = psi(l(u)); for r = 0 put nu = 1. Construct this as a unitary character of H; for quadratic algebras use the additive character on A, equivalently its F-linear trace pairing. For quadratic A require psi_A(x) = psi_F(Tr(A/F)(c x)), with c ∈ Aˣ and psi_F nontrivial; equivalently psi_A is nontrivial on each simple factor. Before conjugacy prove that every flag simple-root coordinate, and both residual coordinates in the split GL description, has a nonzero coefficient.
hypotheses: F is a field with 2 invertible; A is F with identity involution or a quadratic étale F-algebra with its canonical involution; epsilon ∈ {1,−1}; all form modules are finite free and nondegenerate

F is a local field of characteristic different from 2; representations are complex smooth admissible nonarchimedeanly or Casselman–Wallach archimedeanly; all additive characters used are continuous unitary and nontrivial
epsilon = +1, a relevant pair, a Witt flag and the displayed generating vector and factorwise nontrivial character data

locator.where: §12, pp. 44–46; ggp line 1585, ggp line 1624, ggp line 1633

api.name: GGP.besselCharacter_apply

api.name: GGP.besselCharacter_conjugate
api.statement: Different admissible flags, generating e and factorwise nontrivial psi_A give conjugate pairs (H,nu); the simple-root coefficients are nonzero before applying torus conjugation.

api.name: GGP.besselCharacter_baseChange
api.statement: Isometries commuting with the inclusion transport the character; restriction to local fields agrees with the algebraic l-map.

api.name: GGP.besselCharacter_simpleRoots
api.statement: For the displayed admissible data, the flag coordinates and, for A = F × F, both residual GL coordinates carry nontrivial additive characters; in rank-zero flag cases this assertion has no coordinates.

tests.name: bessel_codim_one
tests.statement: With r = 0 the empty sum gives nu = 1; accessing v′0 would be undefined.

tests.name: bessel_two_terms
tests.statement: In split GL coordinates with r = 2 and l(u) = x1 + z, setting (x1,z) = (1,−1) gives nu(u) = 1; using a difference gives psi(2). Choose psi with psi(2) ≠ 1 to make this a negative control.

tests.name: bessel_nonzero_coordinate
tests.statement: In the same additive quotient, (x1,z) = (t,0) with psi(t) ≠ 1 gives nu ≠ 1; the identically trivial character is excluded for r > 0.

tests.name: bessel_split_vector_rejected
tests.statement: For A = F × F, e = (1,0)e0 in a free residual line is nonzero but does not generate L; its norm is zero and in the W = 0, rank-A V = 3 model one GL3 simple-root character vanishes.

tests.name: bessel_split_character_rejected
tests.statement: For A = F × F, psi_A(x,y) = psi_F(x) has trace coefficient c = (1,0), which is not a unit; in the GL3 model it kills one simple-root subgroup even with e = e0.

tests.name: bessel_split_GL3_generic
tests.statement: For W = 0, rank-A V = 3, e = e0 and psi_A(x,y) = psi_F(x+y), choose root coordinates so nu(u) = psi_F(u12+u23); both coefficients are 1 and both root restrictions are nontrivial.

targets.proofSketch: Compute l on products modulo the radical commutator, show its G(W)-invariance, and extend over the semidirect product. Torus conjugation compares the nonzero coordinates.

targets.name: GGP.fourierJacobiQuotient
targets.title: The relative Heisenberg quotient
targets.statement: For epsilon = −1 and rank X > 0, construct the G(W)-equivariant central quotient N(X) → Heis(W,b0), where b0 = 2B for A = F and b0 = Tr(A/F) B for quadratic A/F. The central map is dual to pullback of Hermitian forms along an A-linear surjection ell : X → A (a unimodular functional), and the vector quotient map is that functional tensor id_W. For X = 0 use the identity Jacobi action of G(W) on Heis(W,b0), with no nonexistent functional on X. In the split algebra both component functionals must be nonzero. Prove that ell tensor id_W is onto W and that the F-linear central map is onto F; consequently the group map is surjective.
hypotheses: F is a field with 2 invertible; A is F with identity involution or a quadratic étale F-algebra with its canonical involution; epsilon ∈ {1,−1}; all form modules are finite free and nondegenerate
A relevant skew pair and, when X ≠ 0, an A-linear surjection ell : X → A and a complete isotropic flag whose maximal unipotent fixes ell

locator.where: §12, pp. 47–50; ggp line 1683, ggp line 1703, ggp line 1723, ggp line 1785

api.name: GGP.fourierJacobiQuotient_center
api.statement: The restriction to Z(X) is the dual of pullback along X → A.

api.name: GGP.fourierJacobiQuotient_commutator
api.statement: The image of [u,u′] has central coordinate b0(y(u),y(u′)).

api.name: GGP.fourierJacobiQuotient_equivariant
api.statement: The map commutes with G(W); transport by an isometry is natural.

api.name: GGP.fourierJacobiQuotient_surjective
api.statement: For unimodular ell, both the vector map and central map are surjective, and hence so is N(X) → Heis(W,b0).

tests.name: fj_commutator_two
tests.statement: For A = F, rank X = 1 and B(e,f) = 1 in W, the images of e and f have commutator central coordinate 2; omitting the polar factor gives 1.

tests.name: fj_zero_W
tests.statement: For W = 0 the vector quotient is zero and the Heisenberg group is its center, not a nonzero vector group.

tests.name: fj_no_functional_zero_X
tests.statement: For X = 0 no nonzero functional X → A exists; the codimension-zero construction uses the separate branch.

tests.name: fj_split_idempotent_rejected
tests.statement: For A = F × F, X = A and ell(x) = (1,0)x, ell is nonzero but not onto; its vector image is (1,0)W and its central map is zero since (1,0)conjugate((1,0)) = 0. This is excluded.

tests.name: fj_split_surjection
tests.statement: For X = A and ell = id, both components are nonzero, the vector map is id_W, and pullback on Hermitian lines is the identity, so the central map is onto F.

targets.proofSketch: Identify N(X)/Z(X) with X ⊗ W and its center with Hermitian forms. Compute the commutator pairing before applying Stone–von Neumann. Choose x with ell(x) = 1: w maps back to x tensor w. Pullback of the rank-one unit Hermitian form along ell is injective, so its finite-dimensional F-dual is surjective, including for F × F. Lift a vector coordinate and correct the remaining central coordinate to prove group surjectivity.

targets.name: GGP.fourierJacobiRepresentation
targets.title: Oscillator restriction and auxiliary data
targets.statement: Construct nu = pullback(omega_psi) tensor lambda, with lambda(u) = psi(Tr(sum simple flag coordinates)), extended trivially across G(W). For A = F it is a genuine representation of Htilde = N ⋊ Mp(W); use exactly one genuine factor in the ambient product Sp(V) × Mp(W) or Mp(V) × Sp(W). For a quadratic algebra and a splitting character mu with mu|Fˣ = omega(A/F), obtain an ordinary representation of H. For X = 0 set nu equal to the oscillator representation itself. For X ≠ 0 the pullback uses the surjective quotient of §2.2 and its compatible flag, so its Heisenberg central character is nontrivial.
hypotheses: F is a field with 2 invertible; A is F with identity involution or a quadratic étale F-algebra with its canonical involution; epsilon ∈ {1,−1}; all form modules are finite free and nondegenerate

F is a local field of characteristic different from 2; representations are complex smooth admissible nonarchimedeanly or Casselman–Wallach archimedeanly; all additive characters used are continuous unitary and nontrivial
epsilon = −1; psi nontrivial; mu with the displayed restriction when required

api.name: GGP.fourierJacobiRepresentation_central
api.statement: The nontrivial cover kernel acts by −1; its action on pi tensor nu is +1 for genuine pi.

api.name: GGP.fourierJacobiRepresentation_zero_codim
api.statement: For V = W the flag character is 1 and nu = omega.

api.name: GGP.fourierJacobiRepresentation_changeData
api.statement: Square rescaling of psi in the symplectic case, norm rescaling in the unitary case, and mu′/mu twists agree with the Weil splitting change; state the induced Hom equivalences.

tests.name: fj_genuineness_sign
tests.statement: On pi tensor nu the cover involution acts as (−1)(−1) = 1; on a nongenuine pi tensor nu it acts as −1 and there is no invariant functional.

tests.name: fj_equal_rank
tests.statement: For X = 0 and W nonzero, nu is the restriction of the oscillator representation to the smaller classical group or its cover; its underlying Heisenberg realization has central character psi, but H itself has no Heisenberg subgroup. It is not replaced by 1.

tests.name: fj_zero_small_space
tests.statement: For W = 0 the oscillator factor is one-dimensional and nu reduces to the generic flag character; no mu is needed.

targets.proofSketch: Pull back the imported Weil representation and multiply by the flag character; compare covers by fiber product over the diagonal group. The central involution acts by −1 on both nu and the genuine ambient restriction.

targets.name: GGP.Model
targets.title: Restriction functionals and multiplicity
targets.statement: Define Model(pi,nu) = Hom_H(pi|H tensor nu,C). The functional-space construction allows arbitrary smooth representations before restricting to admissible irreducibles in multiplicity theorems. In the nonarchimedean smooth category use algebraic tensor product and equivariant linear maps; at infinity use completed projective tensor product and continuous linear maps. Define multiplicity as the cardinal dimension over C; under multiplicity one this equals 0 or 1. Never define it by finrank before proving finite dimensionality.
hypotheses: F is a local field of characteristic different from 2; nonarchimedean representations are smooth complex representations, without an admissibility assumption on this construction; archimedean representations have complete nuclear Fréchet spaces and jointly continuous actions, with the Casselman–Wallach subcategory used in the theorems
pi is a representation of the actual ambient group or its required cover, nu is §2.1 or §2.3

locator.where: §14, pp. 57–58; ggp line 2012, ggp line 2036, ggp line 2051

api.name: GGP.Model.mk
api.statement: An invariant bilinear form gives a model; archimedean forms must be jointly continuous.

api.name: GGP.Model.ext
api.statement: Equality of evaluations on pure tensors determines a model, by density and continuity at infinity.

api.name: GGP.Model.congr
api.statement: Representation equivalences and conjugacy of (H,nu) induce linear equivalences of model spaces.

api.name: GGP.Model.algebraicComparison
api.statement: If both pi|H and nu have finite-dimensional Hausdorff complex topological vector spaces with continuous scalar multiplication, the completed/algebraic tensor identification and the pinned intertwiner equivalence identify the continuous and algebraic relative models; on pure tensors the map preserves evaluation.

api.name: GGP.Model.nonzero_iff_multiplicity_ne_zero
api.statement: Nonzero models are equivalent to nonzero cardinal dimension; after the one-dimensional bound, distinction means dimension one.

api.name: GGP.Model.dualConvention
api.statement: For one-dimensional Bessel nu, identify Model(pi,nu) with Hom_H(pi,nu∨); comparison with Hom_H(pi,nu) uses the source’s conjugacy changing nu to nu∨. For nonarchimedean Fourier–Jacobi models supply the corresponding smooth oscillator-dual Hom identification. No archimedean Hom-to-oscillator equality is inferred from an algebraic dual.

tests.name: model_trivial
tests.statement: For H = 1 and pi = nu = C, Model ≅ C and multiplicity = 1.

tests.name: model_zero
tests.statement: If pi is the zero representation, Model = 0 and multiplicity = 0; an unqualified constant-one definition fails.

tests.name: model_sign_character
tests.statement: For the rank-zero symplectic pair use the cover Htilde = Mp(0) = C2 and its genuine oscillator nu = sign. Trivial pi has Model = 0, whereas pi = sign has multiplicity 1. This tests the cover sign on actual relative data.

tests.name: model_infinite_dimension
tests.statement: For H = 1, pi = direct sum of countably many copies of C and nu = C, the algebraic dual is infinite dimensional; finrank would misleadingly return 0.

targets.proofSketch: Specialize existing intertwiner modules to the trivial target. Use the completed tensor universal property only in the topological branch. Forgetting topology is an equivalence only under the finite-dimensional Hausdorff hypotheses of the pinned comparison.

layers.examples: At codimension one the Bessel character is trivial; at codimension zero the Fourier–Jacobi factor is the oscillator representation, rather than a trivial character.

layers.title: Multiplicity one with precise ranges

targets.name: GGP.basicMultiplicityOneNonarchimedean
targets.title: Nonarchimedean basic uniqueness
targets.statement: Over a nonarchimedean characteristic-zero field, the model dimension is at most one for codimension-one Hermitian Bessel pairs (including split quadratic algebra), codimension-one SO pairs, and equal-rank symplectic/metaplectic or skew-Hermitian Fourier–Jacobi pairs. In the last two cases pi has the genuineness and nontrivial oscillator central character of §2.3. Also prove the equivalent Sun Jacobi statement: for irreducible admissible smooth piJ of J(W) and piU of U(W), dim Hom_U(W)(piJ tensor piU,C) ≤ 1 in the skew-Hermitian setting.
hypotheses: F is nonarchimedean of characteristic zero, with no restriction on its residue characteristic
The indicated basic pair; both constituent representations are irreducible admissible smooth

locator.where: Theorem 14.1(ii), p. 58; ggp line 2068; waldspurger Theorem 1, p. 1; waldspurger line 10; sun Theorems B–C, pp. 1–3; sun line 31, sun line 102

tests.name: basic_dyadic

tests.name: basic_SO1

targets.proofSketch: Prove the specialized distribution invariance by descent and Fourier support arguments, then apply the imported Gelfand–Kazhdan criterion. Use Waldspurger’s SO anti-involution rather than transferring O uniqueness to SO without proof. Sun’s Jacobi version and oscillator equivalence give the equal-rank cases.

targets.name: GGP.basicMultiplicityOneArchimedean
targets.title: Archimedean basic uniqueness
targets.statement: For G/G′ equal to GL(n+1,R)/GL(n,R), GL(n+1,C)/GL(n,C), U(p,q+1)/U(p,q), SO(p,q+1)/SO(p,q), or SO(n+1,C)/SO(n,C), invariant continuous bilinear forms on irreducible Casselman–Wallach V × V′ form a space of dimension at most one. For J = G′ ⋉ Heis with G′ equal to GL(n,R), GL(n,C), U(p,q), Sp(2n,R) or Sp(2n,C), the same bound holds for an irreducible Casselman–Wallach psi-representation of J and an irreducible Casselman–Wallach representation of G′, with fixed nontrivial unitary psi on the center.
hypotheses: n,p,q ≥ 0; archimedean groups in the displayed lists
Casselman–Wallach psi-representation means V0 completed-tensor omega_psi with V0 genuine Casselman–Wallach, as in the source

locator.where: Theorems B and C, pp. 2–3; sun-zhu line 55, sun-zhu line 66, sun-zhu line 80, sun-zhu line 94

tests.name: archimedean_zero_rank
tests.statement: For p = q = n = 0 the Jacobi group is its center; a nontrivial psi-character against the trivial smaller group has a one-dimensional bilinear dual.

tests.name: archimedean_topology
tests.statement: Dropping continuity enlarges the functional space on an infinite-dimensional Fréchet space; that enlarged space is outside the theorem.

targets.proofSketch: Prove the source’s anti-automorphism invariance of distributions using descent and Fourier rigidity, then its continuous Gelfand–Kazhdan criterion. Apply the nuclear tensor universal property to compare the bilinear and §2.4 formulations.

targets.name: GGP.besselInductionReduction
targets.title: The Bessel open-orbit reduction
targets.statement: For a nonarchimedean field, W⊥ = X ⊕ E ⊕ X∨ with X ≠ 0 and E a nonisotropic line, put Wplus = V ⊥ (−E), Y = X ⊕ span(e+f). Let tau be supercuspidal of GL(Y), piV,piW irreducible smooth, and I = unnormalized Ind_P(Y)^G(Wplus)(tau external-tensor piW). If piV∨ is in none of the Bernstein components (GL(Y′) × G(V′), tau external-tensor mu) with dim Y′ = dim Y and mu irreducible, construct a linear isomorphism Hom_G(V)(I tensor piV,C) ≅ Hom_H(piV tensor piW,nu). This target covers the full O and unitary groups of the cited theorem; no SO variant is inferred.
hypotheses: F is a local field of characteristic different from 2; representations are complex smooth admissible nonarchimedeanly or Casselman–Wallach archimedeanly; all additive characters used are continuous unitary and nontrivial
F nonarchimedean; the displayed Bernstein exclusion and supercuspidality
In the symmetric trivial-involution case use O in this reduction, as the source does

tests.name: bessel_no_closed_orbit

tests.name: bessel_bad_support
tests.statement: When piV∨ lies in the forbidden component, the closed orbit may contribute; the comparison is not asserted.

targets.proofSketch: Use the open/closed orbit restriction filtration, Bernstein exclusion to kill the closed term, Frobenius reciprocity on the open term and the GL Whittaker quotient. The support-avoidance existence needed to choose tau is part of the local-category contract.

targets.name: GGP.fourierJacobiInductionReduction
targets.title: The Fourier–Jacobi open-orbit reduction
targets.statement: For a nonarchimedean field, W = X ⊕ W0 ⊕ X∨ with X ≠ 0, tau supercuspidal of GL(X), pi0 genuine smooth of Mp(W0), and pi irreducible of Sp(W), form the unnormalized induction Ipsi(tau,pi0) from the inverse image of P(X), using the genuine Levi twist tau tensor chi_psi. If pi∨ belongs to none of the Bernstein components (GL(X) × Sp(W0), tau external-tensor mu), construct Hom_Mp(W)(Ipsi(tau,pi0) tensor pi,omega_W,psi) ≅ Hom_H(pi tensor pi0,nu_W,W0,psi).

F nonarchimedean; tau and the actual Bernstein exclusion as displayed

tests.name: fj_reduction_cover
tests.statement: The kernel involution acts genuinely on both Ipsi and omega; removing chi_psi makes the displayed Hom ill-typed.

targets.proofSketch: Use the mixed oscillator model, evaluation at zero and its nonzero-orbit kernel; the exclusion removes the latter. The source writes a Hom-to-oscillator form: construct its comparison to §2.4 using the actual contragredient conventions, not an archimedean algebraic dual.

targets.name: GGP.MultiplicityOneAssertion
targets.title: The general multiplicity assertion
targets.statement: Define MultiplicityOneAssertion(F,pair,data) as: for every irreducible representation pi in the category of §2.4 with the required genuineness, dim_C Model(pi,nu) ≤ 1. This is a named proposition for every permitted classical pair, distinct from a proof. Theorems §3.1–§3.2 inhabit precisely their ranges; larger-codimension conclusions require a proved reduction valid for that group and field.
hypotheses: F is a local field of characteristic different from 2; representations are complex smooth admissible nonarchimedeanly or Casselman–Wallach archimedeanly; all additive characters used are continuous unitary and nontrivial
A relevant pair and its auxiliary character data

api.name: GGP.MultiplicityOneAssertion.apply

General enhanced theta formulas, including P1, remain owned by MetaplecticAutomorphicForms; P1 is neither an output nor an enhancement prerequisite of this bridge.

targets.name: GGP.unitaryTemperedPacketUniqueness
targets.title: Tempered unitary uniqueness across inner forms
targets.statement: Let F be a characteristic-zero local field different from C and E/F a quadratic field extension. For a Hermitian Bessel GGP triple of odd codimension with both G and its smaller reductive group quasi-split, and every tempered parameter phi, prove that the disjoint union of the packets over the relevant pure inner triples indexed by H1(F,H) contains exactly one representation of multiplicity one. Transport this statement to every relevant complement isometry class admitting such a quasi-split reference triple. At a split quadratic-algebra place, use §4.7. This theorem gives existence and uniqueness, not an explicit epsilon-character theorem at real places. The triple uses the scalar Bessel character of §2.1; this is not a Fourier–Jacobi uniqueness theorem.
hypotheses: F = R or a finite extension of Qp; E/F quadratic field; a Hermitian Bessel reference triple of odd codimension with G and the smaller reductive group quasi-split, and its relevant pure inner triples
The actual tempered packets satisfy stability, transfer with Kottwitz signs, and uniqueness of the prescribed Whittaker model (the source’s STAB, TRANS, WHITT)

targets.proofSketch: Use the local relative trace expansion to express the sum of multiplicities through stable packet characters. Transfer with Kottwitz signs cancels the nonmatching inner terms, and the Whittaker coefficient on the reference form is one. Nonnegative integral multiplicities with total one give a unique member; no explicit enhancement formula is inferred.

targets.name: GGP.GlobalNonvanishingAssertion

targets.name: GGP.orthogonalDelta
targets.title: Orthogonal normalization factors
targets.statement: For a nondegenerate quadratic space of dimension d ≥ 2 define the meromorphic normalization family Delta_SO(d;s) as product(j=1,…,l) zeta(s+2j) if d = 2l+1, and product(j=1,…,l−1) zeta(s+2j) times L(s+l,chi_disc) if d = 2l. Its scalar normalization Delta_SO(d) is the value at s = 0 only where regular. The even discriminant character comes from the square class (−1)^l det Q; use completed functions globally and matching local factors at every place. The global split plane has a pole at s = 0; it has no scalar Delta_SO(2). The period identities use the larger group of dimension at least three, where this pole does not occur.
hypotheses: A global field of characteristic different from 2, or a completion of one; d ≥ 2; nondegenerate Q and its actual discriminant character

targets.name: GGP.orthogonalLocalPeriod
targets.title: Orthogonal matrix-coefficient forms
targets.statement: For a local isometric inclusion V0 ↪ V1 of dimensions n,n+1, n ≥ 2, unitary irreducible admissible pi_i and invariant positive Hermitian pairings, define I_v as the integral over SO(V0)(Fv) of <pi1(t)f1,f1′> times conjugate(<pi0(t)f0,f0′>). Where this integral is absolutely convergent and the local quotient is finite nonzero, define alpha_v = I_v / (Delta_G1,v · L_v(1/2,pi1 tensor pi0) / (L_v(1,pi1,Ad)L_v(1,pi0,Ad))). Keep the meromorphic normalizing L-quotient distinct from the matrix-coefficient integral. At singular normalizing values this construction supplies no scalar alpha; any continued combined value in §7.4 is an explicit clause of the conjecture, rather than a continuation theorem for arbitrary representations.
hypotheses: Fv local of characteristic different from 2; n ≥ 2; forms and inclusion nondegenerate
The ordinary-value alpha requires absolute convergence and regular nonzero normalizing quotient; no scalar alpha or meromorphic family of matrix-coefficient integrals is asserted outside that domain

targets.name: GGP.OrthogonalRefinementAssertions
targets.title: Orthogonal refinement conjectures
targets.statement: For a global adjacent SO pair of dimensions n,n+1 with n ≥ 2 and nonsplit V0 if n = 2, cuspidal irreducible pi_i, define ALG(pi_i) by genericity at almost every place. Under ALG for both and the stipulated meromorphic continuation, define the conjunction of Conjecture 1.4 (every local I converges, is nonnegative on diagonal K-finite vectors, and distinction iff alpha is positive somewhere) and Conjecture 1.5: there exists beta ∈ Z, depending on the representations and normalizations but not vectors or S, such that for all nonzero decomposable vectors satisfying U1–U6 outside finite S, squared period divided by the two Petersson norms equals 2^beta C0 Delta_G1 L(1/2,pi1 tensor pi0)/(L(1,pi1,Ad)L(1,pi0,Ad)) times product(v in S) alpha_v/(norm(f1v)² norm(f0v)²). Here period is integral f1(t) conjugate(f0(t)), and dTam_0 = C0 product dt_v. The scalar quotient at a singular point means the continued combined expression, with cancellation/regularity included in the assertion, never separate 0/0. Define Conjecture 2.1 separately for everywhere tempered pi_i with elliptic Arthur parameters psi_i: replace 2^beta by 1/(abs(S_psi1)abs(S_psi0)), with S_psi the full centralizer in the dual group, not its quotient by the center.
hypotheses: F a global field of characteristic different from 2; all displayed dimension, non-split-plane and ALG hypotheses
pi_i are in actual cuspidal realizations; Tamagawa Petersson pairings; compatible local measures and nonzero decomposable K-finite vectors
The analytic continuation stipulated in ichino-ikeda §1 is part of the assertion’s domain; the tempered coefficient uses actual elliptic Arthur parameters

targets.name: GGP.relativeCharacters
targets.title: The actual relative distributions
targets.statement: Construct the unitary cuspidal relative distribution J_sigma(f) = sum_e Ph(sigma(f)e) conjugate(Ph(e)), over an orthonormal smooth K-basis, and the sum J_X over cuspidal constituents in a specified spectral subset X. Construct the linear distributions I_P,pi and I_Pi from the actual induced automorphic and Whittaker realizations: I_P,pi(f) = sum_e I(Ind(f)e,0) conjugate(J_eta(e)), and I_Pi(f) = sum_W lambda(Pi(f)W) conjugate(beta_eta(W))/<W,W>_Whitt. Here I(e,0) is the regularized Rankin–Selberg period of its Eisenstein series, J_eta the Flicker–Rallis intertwining period, lambda is the continued Whittaker Rankin–Selberg integral at zero, beta_eta is the mirabolic Flicker–Rallis integral with its Asai residue factor, and the Whittaker norm uses the adjoint residue factor; these forms and their measures are the supplier’s constructed analytic objects. Prove the sums are basis-independent continuous distributions and retain this global construction for all the stated cuspidal data. Separately, for tempered sigma_v in the ordinary normalization domain of §7.5, define J_v(fv) = sum_e alpha_v(sigma_v(fv)e,e), using §7.6 and the local trace estimates for absolute convergence, continuity and Cv finite nonzero. Global cuspidality is not a local temperedness hypothesis. Fix dg_Tam on Gh(A), dt_Tam on Hh(A) and positive local measures with product dg_v = dg_Tam and product dt_v = dt_Tam in the convergent restricted-product convention. Define sigma_v(fv) = integral_Gh(Fv) fv(g)sigma_v(g) dg_v and sigma(f) with dg_Tam, so sigma(tensor fv) = tensor sigma_v(fv). The linear distributions use the source differential and finite-S corrections of §8.3; their convolution measure is fixed as part of that source convention.

targets.proofSketch: Factor the linear Whittaker relative character into local factors, identify the Asai denominator with the adjoint denominator, and compare each matching local relative trace. At infinity extend the comparison from the dense transfer subspace by continuity. The real-place packet uniqueness is §5.6 and complex split-place uniqueness is §4.7; neither is inferred from multiplicity one alone. Convert source differential measures dK_v^src for K = Gh,Hh by dK_Tam = (Delta_K^*)⁻¹ product_v Delta_K,v dK_v^src (bpcz §2.3.2). Choose positive a_K,v with convergent product a_K,v = (Delta_K^*)⁻¹ and set dK_v = a_K,v Delta_K,v dK_v^src, standard outside a finite set after convergence factors. Write b_G,v = a_G,v Delta_G,v and b_H,v = a_H,v Delta_H,v. The normalized local distribution becomes b_G,v b_H,v Cv⁻¹ times the source unnormalized local trace. At finite S use dK_Tam = dK_S^src × (Delta_K^(S,*))⁻¹ product_(v outside S) Delta_K,v dK_v^src. The source special tensor is (Delta_Hh^(S,*))² times tensor_(v in S) fsrc_v times tensor_(v outside S) 1_KG,v, and its distribution equals abs(S_Pi)⁻¹ L^S(1/2,Pi_n × Pi_n+1)/L^S(1,sigma,Ad) times product_(v in S) J_sigma_v^raw(fsrc_v) (bpcz line 4891–4892); here the superscript S denotes the outside-S factor, with the leading value at zero on Delta. Passing through finite S and its spherical volumes gives the displayed product-normalized identity, rather than discarding the source leading-value factors. For unitary groups identify Delta_Gh Delta_Hh = Delta_(n+1) (Delta_Hh)², locally and globally; this converts the completed c(sigma) and source partial L-ratio with its squared Hh convergence factor into each other. At each finite S track the outside-S convergence factors as measures, not as an asserted absolutely convergent Euler product at the central point.
